If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1.5–2.5% for the next 5 days to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1.5–2.5% for the next 5 days to account for risk aversion.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in the last 2 days, shift forecast upward by 2–3% for the next 3 days, especially if price is trending upward.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending downward, reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 7 days to reflect weakening momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed and price is trending upward, increase forecast by 1–2% for the next 7 days to reflect bullish sentiment.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is flat, maintain forecast unchanged for next 5 days, but add a 0.5% downward bias if volatility is rising.
